question: A council printed 192 recycling calendars and split them equally among its 4 neighbourhood offices. The north office found 13 of its calendars had pages missing and put them in the bin. Every calendar the north office still had was stapled to 5 information leaflets. The office then had a second identical set of those leaflets printed, so it held 2 times as many leaflets as before. The office car park has 30 spaces. How many leaflets does the north office have?

A creamery filled 110 churns, with 4 buckets of milk going into every churn and 9 litres in every bucket. All of that milk was then run off into containers that each hold 4 litres. The creamery sold 868 of those containers at the Saturday market. A dozen cats sat waiting by the dairy door. The creamery's records are kept in litres rather than in gallons. How many containers are left?

A cycling club owned 132 spare tyres and shared them equally among its 6 branches. The town branch then bought 36 more tyres of its own and was given 18 by a local sponsor. The branch ordered a second identical set, so it ended up holding 2 times as many tyres as it had before the order. Storing a tyre costs the branch 6 cents a week. The club's storage bill is worked out in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents does the town branch pay each week?

An orchard crew picked 188 pears and set aside 18 that were badly bruised. A neighbour brought 5 pears from her own tree to add to the picking crates. All the pears were then packed equally into 5 crates for the market. The stallholder opened one crate and cut every pear in it into 5 slices for the tasting tray. She added 40 slices left over from the day before and 79 that a helper had cut at home. A dozen wasps hovered over the tray all afternoon. How many slices are on the tasting tray?

On Monday morning Layla counted 162 boxes of nails in the depot, with 3 tins in every box and 9 nails in every tin. Later that morning her colleague Marek, who covers a smaller round than Layla does, tipped in 71 loose nails, and before lunch he found 80 more in the back of the van and added those too. In the afternoon 139 bent nails were sorted out and thrown away. In the evening a builder's order took 2029 nails out of the depot. How many nails are left in the depot?

A cobbler had 38 pairs of laces in his drawer and a sales rep left 9 more pairs on the counter. He used 11 pairs on repairs during the week and threw away 3 pairs that had frayed in storage. A shop closing down along the street then sold him 56 pairs cheaply. A dozen customers were waiting outside on the first morning of that sale. The cobbler's till is set in cents rather than dollars. How many pairs of laces are in his drawer?

On Tuesday morning a school kitchen had 30 trays of yoghurt in the fridge, and a delivery added 10 more trays. Before lunch 13 trays were sent over to the infant school down the road. In the afternoon the cook counted 4 rows of pots on every tray still in the fridge, and in the early evening she found 8 pots in each of those rows. Over the following week the children ate 709 pots. The kitchen's order form is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many pots are left?

On Friday morning Hana's food co-op had 231 jars of pickles on the shelves. 150 of them went out on the morning delivery round. Before lunch 22 jars were found with loose lids and were pulled from sale. In the afternoon her partner Ravi, who bottles fewer jars each week than Hana does, brought in 51 jars from his own kitchen, and in the evening a bottling workshop produced 74 more. The co-op's price list is written in cents rather than dollars. How many jars does the co-op have now?

On Wednesday morning a school store held 86 packs of coloured paper, and the art department took 73 of those packs for a project. In the afternoon the office assistant opened what was left and counted 9 sheets in every pack. In the evening the caretaker cut each sheet into 7 strips for the corridor display, and a teacher added 16 strips she had cut at home. How many strips are ready for the display?

On Saturday morning a scout group filled 131 hampers for the food bank, with 8 tins packed in every hamper. Before lunch a supermarket donated 14 loose tins. In the afternoon a church collection added 75 tins to the pile, and in the evening a delivery van brought 64 more. A dozen volunteers were sorting the shelves all day. How many tins does the food bank have?

On Saturday morning a garden centre unloaded 72 boxes of bedding plants, with 5 plants in every box. Later that morning a grower dropped off 72 loose plants at the gate, and at noon a school donated 70 more from its own beds. During the afternoon 164 plants were sold to weekend gardeners. In the evening a landscaper collected an order of 309 plants. How many plants are left at the garden centre?

A quiz club wrote 199 cards for its championship night, and every card carried 4 questions. All the questions were then split equally among the evening's 4 rounds. The host cut 108 questions from the first round because they were too easy for the finalists. Each question left in the first round is worth 3 points, and the winning team also receives a fixed bonus of 79 points. The hall holds 90 people. The score sheet is written in single points rather than in whole rounds. How many points could a team score in the first round including the bonus?

A running club's kit store held 235 race numbers, and a sponsor posted 20 more before the season began. 176 of the numbers were handed out at the summer road race. Every number still in the store was then made up into a race pack with 7 safety pins beside it in the box. At the end the organiser tipped 11 loose pins into the same box. The club's entry list is written in minutes rather than in hours. How many safety pins are in the box?

Nina had 143 minutes of raw footage from the school play and cut 95 minutes of it away. Her editing partner Ross, who had filmed far less than Nina did, handed her 38 minutes from his own camera, and a parent sent in 3 minutes shot on a phone. A second fixed camera contributed 63 minutes, and the sound engineer supplied 28 minutes of backstage clips. The archive is catalogued in minutes rather than in hours. How many minutes of footage does Nina have now?

On Thursday morning a market stall had 127 bread rolls and sold 109 of them before ten o'clock. At lunchtime the baker turned every roll still on the stall into 3 small sandwiches. During the afternoon 33 of those sandwiches were sold to office workers. In the early evening a caterer delivered 64 sandwiches to the same counter, and just before closing a neighbouring stall handed over 39 more. How many sandwiches are on the counter?

On Monday morning a leisure centre had 151 lockers in use by its members. During the morning 23 of them were emptied and closed. In the afternoon 18 new members took lockers of their own, and in the early evening a further 5 were taken. That night the caretaker stuck 6 fresh labels on every locker that was in use. How many labels did the caretaker use?

An apiary keeps 148 hives on the hillside, and every hive holds 9 frames. Each frame is divided into 7 panels, and every panel is fitted with 4 wax strips. The beekeeper also has 6 spare wax strips lying in the shed. The apiary is 3 kilometres from the village. How many wax strips does the apiary have altogether?

On Friday morning a pottery stall had 125 mugs on display and a kiln delivery added 35 more. Before lunch a hotel buyer took 121 mugs for the restaurant. In the afternoon the workshop sent 73 fresh mugs down to the stall. In the evening the owner tripled the stall's stock ready for the weekend craft fair. How many mugs are on the stall now?

On Saturday morning Fatima counted 115 cupcakes on her tray, and her co-baker Leo brought 65, fewer than Fatima had made. Before noon they divided all the cupcakes equally among the 3 charity stalls in the square. In the afternoon a neighbour gave the first stall 23 extra cupcakes. In the evening every cupcake on that first stall was topped with 6 sugar flowers, and a spare box supplied 76 more flowers for the display board. A dozen balloons were tied to the stall's corner post. How many sugar flowers were used at the first stall?

On Wednesday morning a beach kiosk took in 129 packs of ice lollies, with 7 lollies in every pack. Before lunch a supplier added 80 loose lollies to the freezer. In the afternoon the owner decided to give 4 loyalty stamps away with every lolly in the freezer, and in the evening she printed 54 extra stamps to keep behind the counter. How many loyalty stamps did she prepare?

On Saturday morning a raspberry farm had 161 trays ready in the barn and sent 91 of them straight to the supermarket. Before noon the pickers worked out that 7 punnets could be filled from every tray still on the farm. During the afternoon each of those punnets was filled with 6 raspberries. In the evening all the raspberries were divided equally among the 5 jam pans, and the cook tipped 73 more from the cold store into the first pan. How many raspberries are in the first pan?

On Friday morning a hardware store had 194 tins of paint on the shelves, and a delivery added 34 more. Before lunch 37 tins were sold to weekend decorators. In the afternoon a decorating firm bought 148 tins for a contract. In the evening the manager found that 3 sample pots could be filled from every tin still on the shelf, and 115 of those sample pots were sent off to a trade show. The store's sign above the door is 6 metres wide. How many sample pots are left?

A jam factory packed 222 boxes with 4 jars in every box, and the sample room added 74 loose jars to the store. A supermarket order then took 698 jars away, and 60 jars came back when another order was cancelled. Each jar in the store holds 9 spoonfuls of jam. The factory chimney is 30 metres tall. The recipe book is written in grams rather than in kilograms. How many spoonfuls of jam are in the store?

Kofi had 19 model cars on his shelf, and his cousin Amara gave him 69, far more than he had collected himself. He then found 5 more in a box in the attic. He sold 63 of the cars at a car boot sale one Sunday, and bought 38 at a collectors' fair the following month. On his way home he gave 1 to his neighbour's son. How many model cars does Kofi have now?

A council depot had 178 bags of grit at the start of winter. A supplier delivered 17 bags, a neighbouring depot sent over 70, and a farmer returned 9 he had never used. The gritting lorries got through 234 bags during the long cold spell, and 13 bags split open in the rain and were wasted. The depot's records are kept in single bags rather than in tonnes. How many bags of grit are left?
